item_arguments.argument: Use compact interior truncations, the bounded Riemann-to-Lebesgue result, monotone convergence, and the Beta-Gamma identity.
Partition by the success-index subset and sum the independent Bernoulli probabilities, including n=0.
Scale the Euler Gamma integral by t=bx under Countable Choice and normalize the shape-rate kernel.
Reparameterize the scalar Poisson law by exposure times rate; preserve the zero-exposure point mass.
Define the conjugate-form prior only when its parameter-measure normalizer is finite and positive.

Identify the maximum-metric topology with the finite-product topology, transfer Euclidean completeness through the uniform metric inequalities, and use countable rational density to exhibit a Polish presentation.
Define the nonnegative coordinate-simplex density kernel with Gamma factors and declare its reference measure.
Apply the finite multinomial theorem to the probability vector, checking n=0 and zero coordinates.
Prove the Schur complement is PSD, subtract the regression residual, use Gaussian block independence, and verify the conditional-kernel identity.
Construct the IID product density, factor its likelihood ratio through the sum statistic, and apply the standard-Borel common-reference criterion under AC.
Define the Beta law using the proved finite-positive Beta kernel normalizer; state the open-interval convention.
Define Gamma in shape-rate convention using the proved positive finite Gamma density integral.
Use the stick-breaking diffeomorphism, compute its Jacobian, factor into Beta integrals, and cancel Gamma factors.
Define the count-vector mass on the finite admissible support and cite its normalization lemma.
Define the proper Dirichlet law using the proved simplex normalization; include the deterministic k=1 case.
Multiply the normalized Beta prior and Binomial likelihood; integrate the updated kernel and normalize only at finite-positive evidence, including endpoints.
Separate impossible zero-exposure data, multiply likelihood and prior kernels, and use the Gamma integral with total count and exposure.
Multiply the IID exponential-family likelihood and conjugate-form prior; calculate evidence and posterior only on finite-positive evidence fibers.
Separate k=1, multiply the Dirichlet and Multinomial kernels, apply simplex normalization, then normalize the posterior.
Multiply the Gaussian prior and IID likelihood, complete the square, evaluate evidence, and identify posterior parameters.
Construct a jointly Gaussian state/observation pair with singular state covariance and SPD observed covariance, then apply the conditioner.
Substitute a concrete prior and count into the update formulas; calculate endpoint posteriors.
Substitute one positive and one zero exposure into the update and verify an impossible zero-exposure count.
Compute pooled precision and posterior mean for two observations under a proper Gaussian prior.
Evaluate one three-category evidence ratio and record its updated Dirichlet vector.
